current_disclosures.section: Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies > Cash and Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities
current_disclosures.summary: The company defines cash equivalents as highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less, while marketable securities include debt investments with maturities greater than three months and publicly-held equity securities, both classified as current based on their nature and availability for current operations.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 disclosure explicitly expands the definition of marketable securities to include 'publicly-held equity securities,' whereas the 2024 disclosure defined them only as 'highly liquid debt investments.' This represents a meaningful change in the scope of assets classified and managed under this accounting policy.

comparisons.peer_summary: Cash equivalents are defined as financial instruments that are readily convertible into cash and have original maturities of three months or less at the time of purchase.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVDA define cash equivalents using the identical three-month original maturity threshold for instruments readily convertible into cash. However, NVDA explicitly categorizes marketable securities as debt investments with maturities greater than three months and classifies these investments as current based on their availability for current operations, whereas AMD's cited disclosure for this specific item focuses solely on the definition of cash equivalents without detailing the marketable securities classification in the same sentence structure.

sentences.text: We consider all highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into cash and have an original maturity of three months or less at the time of purchase to be cash equivalents.

Cash equivalents consist of financial instruments that are readily convertible into cash and have original maturities of three months or less at the time of purchase.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company considers all highly liquid investment securities with original maturities of three months or less at the date of purchase to be cash equivalents and determines their classification at the time of purchase.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO aligns with NVDA on the three-month original maturity criterion for defining cash equivalents among highly liquid investment securities. Similar to NVDA, AVGO emphasizes determining the appropriate classification at the time of purchase, mirroring NVDA's focus on the nature of investments and their availability for current operations to classify them as current.

comparisons.peer_topic: Classification and accounting of debt investments
comparisons.peer_summary: Debt investments include corporate, government, and financial institution instruments, classified as cash equivalents if matured in three months or less, or as short-term investments if longer or economically hedged. Unhedged debt investments are subject to impairment reviews, with allowances for credit losses recognized in interest and other, net if it is more likely than not the investment will be sold before recovery.
comparisons.comparison: INTC uses the same three-month maturity benchmark as NVDA to classify unhedged debt investments as cash equivalents. In contrast to NVDA's broader description of marketable securities as 'highly liquid debt investments', INTC specifies that debt investments include corporate, government, and financial institution instruments and further distinguishes that investments with maturities greater than three months are classified as short-term investments available for current operations, while also introducing specific impairment and credit loss policies not present in NVDA's definition statement.

sentences.text: We consider all highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into cash and have an original maturity of three months or less at the time of purchase to be cash equivalents.
Marketable securities consist of highly liquid debt investments with maturities of greater than three months when purchased.
Unhedged debt investments with original maturities of approximately three months or less from the date of purchase are classified within cash and cash equivalents.

Unhedged debt investments with original maturities at the date of purchase greater than approximately three months and all economically hedged debt investments are classified as short-term investments, as they represent the investment of cash available for current operations.

comparisons.peer_summary: Cash equivalents are defined as highly liquid short-term investments with original maturities of three months or less that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash. Other investments are classified as short-term if they have remaining maturities of less than one year, and as long-term marketable investments if remaining maturities exceed one year.
comparisons.comparison: MU defines cash equivalents similarly to NVDA, requiring highly liquid short-term investments with original maturities of three months or less that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash. A key difference is that MU explicitly distinguishes between short-term investments (remaining maturity less than one year) and long-term marketable investments (remaining maturity greater than one year), whereas NVDA groups marketable securities generally as debt investments with maturities greater than three months classified as current.
